productBoundary: General city-harbor forecast anchored to public piers, breakwalls, catwalks and immediately adjacent river-mouth shore; boat-only, offshore-only, inaccessible detached structures and upstream-only evidence do not admit a pairing.

sources.title: Great Lakes creel estimate dashboard, preserved Pier/Dock extract
sources.geography: Frankfort-Elberta, Grand Haven, Ludington and Manistee ports
sources.relevantParaphrase: Port-by-month catch estimates and all-species angler hours establish recurrence and broad seasonal concentration for pier/dock mode.
sources.limitations: Port-level rather than exact-structure; all-species effort is not directed effort; omitted rows are not assumed zero; survey does not cover winter consistently; estimates are not catch probabilities.
sources.supports: Candidate admission, recurrence, seasonal timing and conservative relative ceilings

sources.title: Roadmap to Fishing Lake Michigan: Meet your Match!
sources.relevantParaphrase: The DNR identifies burbot as a January-March Ludington target and a February-March Manistee target, while also providing the port-level seasonal context for existing fisheries.
sources.limitations: Explicitly non-exhaustive; does not identify exact pier face, effort, method or magnitude; port opportunity does not authorize boat-only transfer.
sources.supports: Burbot local identity and winter timing

sources.title: Roadmap to Fishing Lake Huron: Get Hooked on Huron!
sources.relevantParaphrase: Harbor Beach is listed for Atlantic salmon, coho, lake trout, smallmouth bass, steelhead and walleye in spring, with lake trout, smallmouth, steelhead and walleye in summer and Atlantic, lake trout, steelhead and walleye in fall. Oscoda lists spring pike and Port Sanilac lists spring mixed salmonids, summer lake trout/steelhead/walleye/white bass and fall salmon/trout/walleye.
sources.limitations: Explicitly non-exhaustive; target timing is coarse and port-wide rather than an exact pier catch rate.
sources.supports: Lake Huron admission and seasonal mode shape

sources.title: Better Fishing Waters
sources.relevantParaphrase: DNR biologists identify Harbor Beach, Port Sanilac and Lake Huron at Oscoda as good fishing locations for named species, including Port Sanilac yellow perch and Oscoda lake whitefish.
sources.limitations: Candidate discovery only unless paired with public shore/pier targetability and timing; mixed modes are not separated.
sources.supports: Candidate identity and corroboration

sources.title: Weekly Fishing Report methods and current report portal
sources.relevantParaphrase: Reports synthesize observations from creel clerks and DNR staff over the prior week.
sources.limitations: Qualitative snapshots; silence is not absence and reports do not standardize target effort.
sources.supports: Authority and interpretation of dated weekly reports

sources.title: 2026 Michigan Fishing Regulations
sources.geography: Michigan Great Lakes and connected waters
sources.relevantParaphrase: Great Lakes trout and salmon are open all year under the applicable table. Lower Peninsula Great Lakes walleye and northern pike, yellow perch, sunfishes, white bass, cisco/whitefish, burbot and other species are open all year; bass is catch-and-immediate-release outside its possession season.
sources.limitations: Anglers must verify current rules and water-specific exceptions; regulation validity must be refreshed after 2027-03-31.
sources.supports: Season and possession gates

sources.title: Fisheries Order 202.26, Special Hook Size Regulations
sources.relevantParaphrase: Within the defined Grand Haven port, only one single-pointed unweighted hook no larger than one-half inch point-to-shank is allowed during November.
sources.limitations: This changes lawful methods, not biological presence; Pass 2 must surface the restriction and must not use historical snagging harvest as lawful bite magnitude.
sources.supports: Grand Haven hard regulation/method gate

sources.title: Things to do: Perch, Salmon & Walleye Fishing
sources.species: yellow perch, salmon, walleye, lake trout
sources.relevantParaphrase: The village explicitly says boatless anglers can catch perch, salmon, walleye and lake trout from the breakwall.
sources.limitations: Promotional municipal source; no catch rate or fine seasonal resolution; local access restrictions still apply.
sources.supports: Public access and targetability for four Port Sanilac groups

sources.title: Ordinance 2025-3: Harbor Rules and Regulations
sources.relevantParaphrase: The harbor ordinance governs access and conduct within the municipal harbor; forecasts must stay scoped to lawful public fishing areas rather than treating every dock or basin edge as public access.
sources.limitations: Operational/access evidence rather than biological evidence; users must follow posted closures and harbor personnel.
sources.supports: Port Sanilac access limitation and product-boundary gate

sources.title: Weekly Fishing Report, August 4, 2021
sources.relevantParaphrase: A good number of bluegills were caught from the pier with redworms.
sources.limitations: One dated qualitative event; magnitude and recurrence come from the creel extract.
sources.supports: Exact pier identity, method and summer timing

sources.title: Weekly Fishing Report, October 19, 2017
sources.relevantParaphrase: Pier anglers caught white perch and channel catfish on minnows.
sources.limitations: One dated event; local recurrence and summer concentration come from the creel extract.
sources.supports: Exact pier identity, method and fall shoulder

sources.title: Ports of Grand Haven, Muskegon and Whitehall/Montague under single-pointed hook regulations Nov. 1-30
sources.relevantParaphrase: DNR calls the spawning aggregation a unique angler opportunity while reporting that much historical harvest was snagged and that the population is declining.
sources.limitations: Historical harvest cannot calibrate lawful bite magnitude; use a low ceiling and the current single-hook restriction.
sources.supports: Admission, autumn timing, conservation and magnitude restraint

sources.title: Weekly Fishing Report, May 4, 2022
sources.species: northern pike, walleye, mixed salmonids and whitefish
sources.relevantParaphrase: Manistee piers produced a few walleye and pike; Frankfort piers produced a mix including walleye and northern pike.
sources.limitations: Qualitative event; unspecified pier side and no standardized effort.
sources.supports: Exact pier identity and spring timing

sources.title: Weekly Fishing Report, April 24, 2024
sources.species: northern pike, walleye, steelhead, yellow perch
sources.relevantParaphrase: Frankfort anglers between the piers caught pike and walleye; Manistee pier anglers reported slow pike and cast for walleye.
sources.limitations: The Frankfort pike/walleye sentence is trolling between piers, within the harbor boundary but not stationary shore casting; qualitative only.
sources.supports: Current recurrence and spring city-harbor timing

sources.title: Weekly Fishing Report, September 17, 2025
sources.species: coho salmon, northern pike, smallmouth bass
sources.relevantParaphrase: Northern pike and smallmouth bass were caught while casting artificial lures in the harbor/breakwall context.
sources.limitations: One event; supports a bounded warm-season mode, not a high annual ceiling.
sources.supports: Harbor Beach pike admission and fall shoulder

sources.title: Weekly Fishing Report, October 18, 2018
sources.relevantParaphrase: Harbor Beach breakwalls produced walleye, consistent with the DNR port roadmap.
sources.limitations: Qualitative snapshot and no effort denominator.
sources.supports: Exact breakwall identity and low-light fall timing

sources.title: Weekly Fishing Report, October 20, 2021
sources.relevantParaphrase: Walleye and a few coho were caught from the breakwall, with early morning and evening best.
sources.limitations: Qualitative snapshot and no effort denominator.
sources.supports: Walleye recurrence, method and diel context

sources.title: Weekly Fishing Report, April 20, 2022
sources.relevantParaphrase: Coho, steelhead and lake trout were in 8-14 feet of water and breakwall anglers caught coho while casting.
sources.limitations: The steelhead and lake-trout sentence includes planer-board fishing and is not exact pier catch proof; it corroborates the roadmap's spring nearshore window.
sources.supports: Spring coldwater accessibility and conservative strength

sources.title: Weekly Fishing Report, April 25, 2013
sources.relevantParaphrase: Anglers casting Cleos from the breakwall took coho and an occasional brown trout.
sources.limitations: Old, single qualitative report and explicitly occasional for brown trout; it establishes occurrence but not a current recurring target fishery.
sources.supports: Harbor Beach brown-trout defer decision and exact-structure occurrence

sources.title: Weekly Fishing Report, May 1, 2014
sources.relevantParaphrase: Shore anglers at the old Edison channel were specifically targeting steelhead.
sources.limitations: One older qualitative report with no catch or effort estimate; useful for target intent and shore accessibility, not magnitude.
sources.supports: Harbor Beach steelhead shore targetability

sources.title: Weekly Fishing Report, May 11, 2022
sources.relevantParaphrase: A couple Atlantic salmon and coho were taken from the breakwall with minnows and small lures.
sources.limitations: One dated event; strength remains bounded by other weekly and roadmap evidence.
sources.supports: Atlantic salmon exact breakwall identity, method and spring timing

sources.title: Weekly Fishing Report, June 15, 2022
sources.relevantParaphrase: Pier anglers caught a few white bass and breakwall anglers caught smallmouth bass.
sources.limitations: White bass counts were small; roadmap supplies the broader summer target window.
sources.supports: White bass and smallmouth exact structure identity

sources.title: Weekly Fishing Report, June 13, 2019
sources.fishingMode: casting body baits and artificial lures
sources.species: walleye, Atlantic salmon, northern pike, smallmouth bass
sources.relevantParaphrase: Breakwall casters caught walleye or Atlantic salmon; shore anglers caught pike and smallmouth bass.
sources.limitations: Combined Lexington/Port Sanilac wording applies to shore pike/smallmouth; only walleye/Atlantic is explicitly Port Sanilac.
sources.supports: Walleye and Atlantic recurrence; pike/smallmouth regional corroboration

sources.title: Weekly Fishing Report, May 29, 2024
sources.geography: Port Sanilac north and south breakwalls
sources.relevantParaphrase: Atlantic salmon and steelhead were caught from both breakwalls.
sources.limitations: Qualitative snapshot and no effort denominator.
sources.supports: Atlantic/steelhead exact-city recurrence

sources.title: Weekly Fishing Report, May 21, 2025
sources.relevantParaphrase: Smallmouth bass were caught from the north breakwall.
sources.limitations: One recent event; summer continuation is corroborated by 2022 and the species' local harbor use.
sources.supports: Smallmouth exact structure and spring shoulder

sources.title: Weekly Fishing Report, October 20, 2021
sources.relevantParaphrase: Breakwall anglers caught occasional steelhead, pike and coho.
sources.limitations: Low qualitative magnitude; supports a shoulder rather than a high peak.
sources.supports: Pike recurrence and fall timing

sources.title: Weekly Fishing Report, September 28, 2022
sources.geography: Lower Au Sable River and mouth at Oscoda
sources.relevantParaphrase: Walleye and northern pike were caught in the lower river while Chinook were caught near the mouth.
sources.limitations: Lower-river/mouth evidence is within the city-harbor product boundary but is not an exact end-of-pier observation.
sources.supports: Oscoda pike fall mode

sources.title: Weekly Fishing Report, April 17, 2024
sources.species: steelhead, Atlantic salmon, lake trout, walleye, brown trout
sources.relevantParaphrase: The pier produced multiple salmonids plus walleye and brown trout.
sources.limitations: Single brown-trout event does not establish a recurring major pairing; the other species are corroborated elsewhere.
sources.supports: Spring identity and the brown-trout defer decision

sources.title: Close to Home Fishing Opportunities
sources.geography: Sheboygan, Port Washington, Milwaukee, Racine and Kenosha public piers/breakwaters
sources.relevantParaphrase: The named structures list the four salmonid species already live; they do not list the proposed non-core additions.
sources.limitations: Species lists are not guaranteed exhaustive and do not establish absence, but omission prevents using this source to admit a new numeric pairing.
sources.supports: Exact public access and conservative Wisconsin roster boundary

sources.title: Lake Michigan Creel Harvest Tables 1998-2024
sources.relevantParaphrase: Southern-county pier lake-trout harvest is sparse and the tables do not provide city-level seasonal non-core target effort.
sources.limitations: County and annual aggregation cannot assign a catch to one city pier or month; harvest omits released fish.
sources.supports: Wisconsin defer/exclude ceilings

sources.title: 2024 Lake Michigan Sport Harvest Report
sources.geography: Wisconsin Lake Michigan and Green Bay survey areas
sources.relevantParaphrase: Mode tables establish that non-core species occur in Wisconsin pier fisheries but do not identify which Lake Michigan city produced them.
sources.limitations: Geographically pooled; reduced sampling and modeled periods; cannot admit a city pairing alone.
sources.supports: Regional corroboration only

sources.authority: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources via Internet Archive
sources.title: Southern Lake Michigan Fishing Reports, July-August 2024
sources.relevantParaphrase: Repeated Kenosha pier and Racine shore perch observations support the yellow-perch pairings already live, but do not establish Milwaukee perch.
sources.limitations: Short qualitative snapshots and archived rolling page; no standardized effort.
sources.supports: No additional Wisconsin admission beyond already-live perch

sources.authority: Seehafer News reproducing the Wisconsin outdoor report
sources.title: Outdoor Report
sources.relevantParaphrase: A few smallmouth bass were reported in a mixed pier catch.
sources.limitations: Secondary reproduction, one old incidental event and no directed effort; insufficient for numeric admission.
sources.supports: Sheboygan smallmouth defer

sources.authority: Harrison et al., Journal of Fish Biology; indexed by PubMed
sources.title: Temporal plasticity in thermal-habitat selection of burbot Lota lota, a diel-migrating winter specialist
sources.relevantParaphrase: Tagged burbot selected below 2 C during spawning and 12-14 C during non-reproductive nighttime feeding.
sources.limitations: Habitat occupancy is not Great Lakes pier bite probability; reservoir population and diel behavior limit direct transfer.
sources.supports: Burbot thermal domain and broad cold-water optimum

sources.title: Temperature preferences and tolerances for Michigan fishes, Fisheries Research Report 2061
sources.species: burbot, bluegill and other catalog species
sources.relevantParaphrase: The report classifies burbot as coldwater and bluegill as warmwater, summarizing good-growth and tolerance ranges.
sources.limitations: Compiled physiology values do not measure angling response; life-stage and source-study differences remain.
sources.supports: Thermal curve domain and cross-check

sources.title: Temperature requirements of Great Lakes fishes, Special Publication 87-3
sources.relevantParaphrase: White perch growth optimum is summarized near 28.5 C with a 26.3-31.7 C growth range and a short-term maximum near 33 C.
sources.limitations: Values include juvenile/specific study contexts and are not a bite curve; northern Great Lakes field behavior may be cooler.
sources.supports: White-perch warmwater center and upper domain

sources.title: White Perch Morone americana species account
sources.relevantParaphrase: White perch spawn in spring around 11-15 C and may remain in freshwater year-round.
sources.limitations: Spawning temperature is not a feeding optimum or local pier catch rate.
sources.supports: Lower thermal shoulder and seasonal biology

sources.title: White Bass (Morone chrysops)
sources.relevantParaphrase: White bass spawn in tributaries or rocky lake shoals near 14 C and return to open water after spawning.
sources.limitations: Spawning biology is not a local bite model and cannot set city strength.
sources.supports: White-bass lower thermal shoulder and mode interpretation

sources.authority: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency literature review
sources.title: White Bass temperature data from laboratory and review studies
sources.relevantParaphrase: The review reports a cooler migration range, a broad spawning range, and a much warmer adult preferred range, requiring a broad rather than narrow global compatibility plateau.
sources.limitations: Underlying references and contexts differ; no value is a Great Lakes pier bite optimum.
sources.supports: White-bass thermal domain and broad plateau

sources.title: Bluegill species account
sources.relevantParaphrase: Bluegills favor 64-70 F water with cover and spawn shallow when water reaches about 65 F.
sources.limitations: General habitat guidance is not a pier-specific feeding response; local strength comes from Grand Haven evidence.
sources.supports: Bluegill lower optimum shoulder and warm-season behavior
